description:
<p><strong>Contrasting color</strong> is a yarn color that is intentionally different from the main or background color so it stands out clearly in the finished fabric.</p>

<p>In machine knitting, a contrasting color is often used to:</p>

<ul>

<li>Emphasize borders, cuffs, bands, or hems</li>

<li>Create stripes, motifs, or text that are easy to see</li>

<li>Highlight design details such as pockets, button bands, or decorative seams</li>

<li>Add a temporary marker, marker row, or separator to make shaping steps easy to spot while knitting</li>

</ul>

<p>A color can contrast by being lighter or darker, a different hue (for example, blue against orange), or much more or less saturated than the main color. For the strongest effect, choose a contrasting color that is clearly different in value (light vs dark) so the stitch pattern and shapes are easy to see from a distance.</p>

<p>Patterns may abbreviate contrasting color as <strong>CC</strong> and main color as <strong>MC</strong>.</p>
tooltip: A clearly different yarn color used for standout details or temporary marker rows in your knitting.
example: Knit 2 rows in CC for stripe afd
